subject: Hosted plan phase lift and rate harmonization
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>
To: Miguel Torres <miguel@ellutech.com>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com, marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted plan phase lift and rate harmonization

Hi Miguel —

Thanks again for the time last week. As ElluTech approaches the next phase of your feature rollout, I wanted to put a concrete, short proposal on the table so your team can lock in budget and runway. High level: a 30% uplift to your current monthly commit, with a two‑tier usage band that gives you a lower unit rate up to 1.2x committed usage and a modestly higher rate in the burst band. This keeps predictable costs for the steady state and limits tail spend during spikes.

Key elements I recommend:
- Monthly commit: move from 1.0M tokens/month to 1.3M tokens/month (30% uplift)
- Banding: base rate applies to 0–1.2x commit; burst rate applies 1.2x–2.0x, with per-token caps
- Short migration window: 60 days to transition so we don’t interrupt your staging jobs
- Ops: a single ops runbook handoff and one two-hour runbook walkthrough (attached)
- Commercial: standard 12‑month term; we can discuss a 24‑month discount if you want longer price stability

I attached the updated rate card and a lightweight runbook for the ops handoff. If this looks reasonable I can loop in Procurement and generate an addendum (DocuSign) with the new tiers and the migration timeline.

Two asks for today: (1) confirm whether the 60‑day migration window works for you, and (2) tell me who on your side will own the procurement conversation so I can copy them on the addendum.

Thanks — looking forward to continuing the momentum.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com
Attachment: redwood-rate-card-v2.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)
Attachment: ops-runbook.xlsx (XLSX, 350KB)

From: Miguel Torres <miguel@ellutech.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted plan phase lift and rate harmonization

Naomi —

Appreciate the clear proposal. High level sounds good; procurement will push back on any open‑ended burst exposure, so I like the band concept. Quick notes from our side: 
- 60 days is tight but doable if we start procurement this week.
- Can you confirm the per‑token cap in the burst band? Our CFO needs a maximum monthly liability estimate.
- We need a one‑page summary for our Legal team explaining SLA impacts (if any) and whether the uplift changes retention/audit log behavior.

Procurement lead is Sara Li (sara.li@ellutech.com) — please loop her on the addendum. Also, is there flexibility on a six‑month ramp instead of a hard 60‑day cutover? That would let us shift traffic gradually.

Thanks,
Miguel
Head of Product
ElluTech

Folks — forwarding Miguel's reply. He wants: (a) explicit per‑token cap for the burst band for liability modeling; (b) a one‑pager for Legal on SLA/retention; (c) procurement contact Sara Li and asks about a six‑month ramp as an alternative to the 60‑day cutover.

Notes / suggested responses: 
- Pricing: propose burst cap at $18k/mo (hard cap) in addition to the burst per‑token rate; this preserves the economics while giving the CFO a ceiling.
- Ramp: operationally we can support a six‑month staged ramp with preset throttle thresholds at 1.2x, 1.5x, and 2.0x so we can monitor quality and spend. That will require a short SLA addendum indicating the staged rollback policy.
- Legal one‑pager: I can draft a focused note: no change to data retention or audit logs; SLA latency and availability commitments remain the same; burst band does not change data handling. Marcus — can you confirm there are no surprises for Private/DEDUPE audit paths?

Action items: Marcus to confirm technical/legal ops items; Aditya to draft commercial language with the $18k cap/alternate six‑month ramp pricing. I’ll prepare the one‑pager and the initial addendum template once you confirm.

—Naomi

Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com, marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com
Date: Thu, 14 Oct 2026 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Final: Hosted plan phase lift — addendum and next steps

Miguel / Sara —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per our internal alignment, here’s what we can commit to for the addendum: 

1) Commercial
- Monthly commit: 1.3M tokens/month for 12 months
- Pricing band: base rate up to 1.2x commit; burst rate for 1.2x–2.0x
- Hard monthly liability cap: $18,000 in burst spend beyond the base band (once reached, traffic will be throttled to base flow until the next billing period unless you request and approve an emergency override)

2) Migration cadence (choose one)
- Option A (fast): 60‑day migration window with full traffic cutover at day 61; includes two runbook sessions
- Option B (staged): six‑month ramp with thresholds at 1.2x, 1.5x, 2.0x; includes monthly check‑ins and an automated rollback policy at each threshold if error rates or latency degrade beyond agreed limits

3) Ops / Legal
- No change to data retention, audit logging, or encryption practices; SLA availability and latency SLOs unchanged. I attached a one‑pager for Legal summarizing these points.

Next steps: (1) Sara, please confirm which migration cadence you prefer and whether Procurement needs additional paperwork; (2) Miguel, if all looks good I’ll send the addendum (DocuSign link below) and schedule the first runbook walkthrough.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/sign/abc123-ellutech
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/1142

Thanks — we’ll make the addendum short and focused so you can get it to Legal/Finance quickly.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
